examples.en: After taking a break from studying, my skills went backward.
This country's economy is regressing.
If you stay still, you actually fall behind.

examples.ko: 기술이 퇴보하지 않도록 계속 연구해야 해요.
examples.en: We have to keep researching so that the technology doesn't regress.
Many people worry that society is regressing.
I practice a little every day for fear of falling back.

explain: '발전하다'의 반대말이에요. 실력, 경제, 기술, 사회처럼 비교적 큰 대상이 나빠질 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '실력이 떨어졌어요'라고 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: If you practice every day, your skills won't decline.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 나빠지지 않는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form means things do not get worse.

phrases.en: After taking a break, I was surprised at how much my skills had regressed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형 관형사형으로 명사를 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past modifier form describes a noun.

phrases.en: After taking a break from exercise, my ability dropped.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 훨씬 자주 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A much more common and easier everyday expression.

explain_en: It is the opposite of '발전하다' (to progress). It is used for fairly big subjects such as skills, the economy, technology and society getting worse. In daily conversation people often say '실력이 떨어졌어요'.

en: to fizzle out; to peter out

examples.ko: 처음엔 열심히 하더니 프로젝트가 흐지부지돼 버렸어요.
examples.en: They worked hard at first, but the project just fizzled out.
The promised repair petered out, so I inquired again.
My diet plan fizzled out before I knew it.

examples.ko: 회의에서 나온 이야기가 흐지부지될까 봐 걱정돼요.
examples.en: I'm worried that what was discussed in the meeting will come to nothing.
The club meetings are gradually fading away.

examples.ko: 이번 사건 조사가 흐지부지되면 안 돼요.
examples.en: The investigation of this case must not just fizzle out.

explain: 끝맺음이 분명하지 않게 슬그머니 사라질 때 써요. 일상에서는 '흐지부지 끝나다', '흐지부지 넘어가다'처럼 부사 '흐지부지'로도 많이 말하고, 계획·약속·조사·모임에 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: It's a pity that the meeting just fizzled out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사 '흐지부지'를 써서 끝이 분명하지 않게 끝나는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the adverb '흐지부지' for something ending without a clear finish.

phrases.en: You shouldn't just let the problem slide.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제를 분명히 해결하지 않고 슬쩍 지나가는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means passing over a problem without properly dealing with it.

phrases.example: 이번 계획은 흐지부지되지 않게 끝까지 해요.
phrases.en: Let's see this plan through so it doesn't fizzle out.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 않게'와 함께 써서 흐지부지되는 것을 막자는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Combined with '-지 않게' to mean preventing it from fizzling out.

explain_en: Passive-type (-되다): a plan or effort fizzles out by itself, without anyone deciding to stop. It is used when something fades away without a clear ending. In daily speech people also use the adverb '흐지부지' as in '흐지부지 끝나다' or '흐지부지 넘어가다', and it suits plans, promises, investigations and meetings.

t90.ax: My diet plan fizzled out before I knew it.

en: to be delicate-featured; to be pleasant-looking

examples.en: That actor has a delicate, pretty face.
Unlike his refined looks, his personality is spirited.

examples.ko: 동생은 어릴 때 곱상해서 여자아이로 오해받았어요.
examples.en: My brother was so delicate-looking as a kid that he was mistaken for a girl.
He looks gentle and fair, but he is really good at sports.
I was complimented for looking fair and delicate.
He had a neat, pretty look, so my first impression was good.

explain: '잘생기다'와 달리 얼굴선이 곱고 순한 인상일 때 써요. 남자에게 쓰면 듣는 사람에 따라 남자다운 느낌이 약하다는 말로 들릴 수 있으니 조심하세요. '예쁘장하다'와 비슷하지만 더 얌전하고 단정한 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: My younger brother has a pretty face, so he's popular.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생김새를 말할 때 '곱상하게 생기다'가 자주 쓰여요.
phrases.nuance_en: '곱상하게 생기다' is the common way to talk about someone's looks.

phrases.en: He has a delicate face but a deep voice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 쓰는 활용형으로 순하고 고운 얼굴을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form before a noun describing a soft, fine-featured face.

phrases.en: That child has a pretty face.
phrases.nuance_ko: '곱상하다'와 비슷하지만 주로 여자아이나 어린 사람에게 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 곱상하다 but most often used for girls or young people.

explain_en: Unlike '잘생기다', it is used for a face with soft, delicate lines and a gentle look. Said about a man, some listeners may hear it as 'not very masculine', so be careful. It is similar to '예쁘장하다' but feels more modest and neat.

t90.ax: That actor has a delicate, pretty face.

en: to be completely exhausted; to be absolutely worn out

examples.en: I walked on mountain trails all day and I'm completely worn out.

examples.ko: 시험이 끝나고 나니 기진맥진해서 말도 안 나와요.
examples.en: After the exam, I'm so exhausted I can't even speak.
The exhausted children fell asleep in the car.
I didn't know I would be this worn out.
After working all night, I'm always completely drained.
When I'm totally exhausted, I don't want to do anything.

explain: '피곤하다'나 '지치다'보다 힘이 완전히 빠진 상태를 강조해요. 달리기, 등산, 야근처럼 몸을 많이 쓴 뒤에 어울려요. '녹초가 되다'도 비슷해요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling came home looking completely exhausted.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 말로 지친 모습을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, it describes an exhausted appearance.

phrases.en: I was so exhausted that I couldn't climb the stairs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지친 이유를 말하고 뒤에 결과를 이어 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to give exhaustion as the reason for what follows.

phrases.en: I'm so tired today because I had a lot of work.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기진맥진하다'보다 약하고 일상에서 두루 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Milder than '기진맥진하다' and widely used in daily life.

explain_en: It stresses that all your strength is gone, stronger than '피곤하다' or '지치다'. It suits times after heavy physical effort such as running, hiking or overtime. '녹초가 되다' is similar.

en: to be skinny; to be bony

examples.ko: 그 배우는 요즘 너무 깡말라 보여요.
examples.en: That actor looks too skinny these days.
He has a bony build, but he is really strong.
My younger brother is so skinny that Mom always worries.
I dieted too hard and became gaunt.

examples.ko: 깡마르다고 해서 건강하지 않은 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Being very thin doesn't mean being unhealthy.
The old man was very thin, but his eyes were sharp.

explain: '마르다'보다 훨씬 심하게 뼈가 드러날 만큼 여윈 모습이에요. '날씬하다'와 달리 칭찬이 아니에요. 'ㄹ' 때문에 '깡말라요', '깡마른'처럼 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: After being sick, my face became gaunt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얼굴이나 몸이 뼈가 보일 만큼 여윈 모습이에요. '깡마른'으로 명사를 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: A face or body so thin that bones show. '깡마른' modifies a noun.

phrases.en: The cat is skin and bones, as if it hasn't eaten for days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 'ㄹ' 때문에 '깡말랐어요'로 바뀌어요. 지금 상태가 아주 말랐다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Because of the 'ㄹ' it becomes '깡말랐어요'. It says someone is extremely thin now.

phrases.en: I've lost a lot of weight lately because of work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쉬운 비슷한 말이에요. '깡마르다'보다 훨씬 약하고 중립적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, similar phrase. It is much milder and more neutral than '깡마르다'.

explain_en: It is much stronger than '마르다' and means so thin that the bones show. Unlike '날씬하다', it is not a compliment. Because of the ㄹ, it changes to forms like '깡말라요' and '깡마른'.

t90.ax: I dieted too hard and became gaunt.

en: to be rough; to be stubbly

examples.en: I woke up and my face looks haggard.
My hair was rough, so I bought a treatment.
His face has become quite haggard in a few days.
I feel bad touching the baby with my rough hands.
I was tired and went to work looking worn out.
I washed a puppy with coarse fur.

explain: '거칠다'와 비슷하지만, 얼굴이나 피부가 마르고 윤기가 없어서 피곤해 보인다는 느낌이 자주 들어가요. '얼굴이 꺼칠해지다'는 건강이 안 좋아 보일 때 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.example: 어제 야근을 해서 오늘 얼굴이 꺼칠해 보여요.
phrases.en: I worked late yesterday, so my face looks haggard today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피곤하거나 건강이 좋지 않아서 얼굴이 거칠고 지쳐 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a face looks rough and worn out from tiredness or poor health.

phrases.en: A moisturizing cream is good for rough skin.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ'을 붙여 거칠고 윤기 없는 피부를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form describes skin that is rough and dull.

phrases.en: I caught a cold and my face looks worn out.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아지다'를 붙여 상태가 나빠졌다는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-아지다' it means the condition has gotten worse.
phrases.en_equiv: for one's face to look worn

explain_en: It is similar to '거칠다' (rough), but often carries a sense of dry, dull skin that makes someone look tired. '얼굴이 꺼칠해지다' is what you say when someone looks unwell.

en: to be spotless; to be impeccable; to be unhurt

examples.en: I played all night, but my mind is still clear.

examples.ko: 넘어졌는데 다친 데 없이 몸이 말짱했어요.
examples.en: I fell down, but my body was fine without any injury.

examples.ko: 세탁했는데도 옷이 말짱한 걸 보니 소재가 좋은가 봐요.
examples.en: The clothes look fine even after washing, so the fabric must be good.
The computer that was working fine suddenly shut off.
You said you were sick, but your face looks perfectly fine.

examples.ko: 겉은 말짱해 보여도 속은 다 상했어요.
examples.en: It looks intact on the outside, but it's all spoiled inside.

explain: '멀쩡하다'와 비슷하게 다치거나 망가진 데 없이 온전할 때 써요. '정신이 말짱하다'처럼 졸리거나 흐릿하지 않고 또렷하다는 뜻으로도 많이 말해요. 사람의 몸, 물건, 정신 상태에 두루 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: The cars collided, but the people are fine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말짱하다와 비슷하고 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 말짱하다 and more common in daily talk.

phrases.en: My cold is all gone and I feel fine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아프거나 다친 데가 없이 괜찮은 몸 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a body with no illness or injury.

phrases.en: I drank coffee, so my mind is clear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 졸리거나 흐릿하지 않고 정신이 또렷할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used when your mind is clear, not sleepy or foggy.

explain_en: Like '멀쩡하다', it is used when something or someone is intact, without injury or damage. It is also commonly used for a clear mind, as in '정신이 말짱하다', meaning not sleepy or hazy. It works for a person's body, objects and mental state.

examples.en: I had a simple procedure at the dermatology clinic.

examples.ko: 이 시술은 흉터가 거의 안 남아요.
examples.en: This procedure leaves almost no scar.

examples.ko: 시술 후에는 일주일 동안 운동하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: After the procedure, you shouldn't exercise for a week.
How much would the procedure cost?

examples.ko: 어머니는 눈 시술을 받고 훨씬 편해지셨어요.
examples.en: My mother felt much better after getting an eye treatment.

examples.ko: 어떤 시술이 저한테 맞을지 의사 선생님께 여쭤봤어요.
examples.en: I asked the doctor which procedure would suit me.

explain: '수술'은 몸을 크게 열어서 하는 치료이고, '시술'은 피부를 조금만 건드리거나 주사·레이저로 하는 가벼운 치료에 많이 써요. 보통 '시술을 받다', '시술을 하다'로 말해요. 병원 광고에서는 피부·미용 이야기에 특히 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I had a procedure at the hospital yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치료를 받는 사람이 쓰는 가장 기본적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase for the person receiving the treatment.

phrases.en: After the procedure, be careful when washing your face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치료가 끝난 뒤를 말해요. 병원 안내에서 자주 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the time after treatment. Often heard in hospital instructions.

phrases.en: The procedure takes about thirty minutes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치료에 걸리는 시간을 말할 때 써요. 예약할 때 많이 물어봐요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for how long the treatment takes. A common question when booking.

explain_en: 수술 (surgery) usually means opening the body, while 시술 is used for lighter treatments done with injections, lasers, or tiny cuts. People say '시술을 받다' (to get a procedure) or '시술을 하다' (to perform one). You will see it a lot in clinic ads, especially for skin and beauty treatments.

en: to be active; to be vigorous

examples.en: My grandfather is still active and energetic.
Kids have a hearty appetite, so they eat a lot.
When spring comes, the trees grow vigorously.

examples.ko: 그 작가는 왕성한 창작 활동으로 유명해요.
examples.en: That writer is famous for his prolific creative work.

examples.ko: 호기심이 왕성한 학생이 질문을 많이 해요.
examples.en: A student with great curiosity asks many questions.
You have to be healthy for your stamina to be strong.

explain: '왕성하다'는 식욕, 호기심, 활동처럼 힘이 넘쳐서 활발할 때 써요. '건강하다'는 몸 상태 전체를 말하고, '왕성하다'는 그 힘이 눈에 띄게 드러난다는 느낌이 있어요. 보통 '식욕이 왕성하다', '왕성한 활동'처럼 짝이 정해져 있어요.

phrases.example: 아이들은 왕성한 호기심으로 질문을 많이 해요.
phrases.en: Children ask many questions out of their strong curiosity.
phrases.nuance_ko: 호기심이 아주 많고 활발할 때 쓰는 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical pairing for very active, abundant curiosity.

phrases.en: My appetite has grown strong since I started exercising.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래보다 입맛이 더 좋아졌다는 변화를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a change where the appetite gets stronger.

phrases.en: Thanks to the spring rain, the grass grows vigorously.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식물이 힘 있게 잘 자랄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when plants grow vigorously.

explain_en: Strong, vigorous energy, often of activity or appetite (활동이 왕성하다) '왕성하다' is used when appetite, curiosity or activity is overflowing with energy. '건강하다' describes overall condition, while '왕성하다' implies the vitality is clearly visible. It usually pairs with fixed words, as in '식욕이 왕성하다' or '왕성한 활동'.

t90.ax: My grandfather is still active and energetic.

examples.en: We climbed the mountain in extreme cold.
The athlete pushed his body to the limit.
My patience reached its limit.
He acted calmly even in an extreme situation.
It was a challenge that went beyond the limit.
He crossed the desert fighting against the extremes.

explain: '한계'는 넘기 어려운 선이고, '극한'은 그 선에 거의 닿은 가장 심한 상태예요. '극한의 추위', '극한 직업'처럼 어려움이 아주 클 때 붙여요. 수학에서는 다른 뜻의 용어로도 나와요.

phrases.en: Firefighting is an extremely tough job.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 힘들고 위험한 일을 말할 때 쓰는 인기 있는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A popular phrase for extremely hard or dangerous work.

phrases.en: You have to stay calm even in extreme situations.
phrases.nuance_ko: 견디기 어려운 아주 심한 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a very severe situation that is hard to bear.

phrases.en: The extreme heat made it hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: '극한의' 뒤에 더위, 추위 같은 말을 붙여 정도를 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '극한의' before words like heat or cold stresses the degree.

explain_en: '한계' is a line that is hard to cross, while 극한 is the most severe state, almost at that line. It is attached as in '극한의 추위' (extreme cold) or '극한 직업' (an extremely tough job). In math it is also a term with a different meaning.

en: to be quick; to be speedy; to be swift

examples.en: Our cat is really quick.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 몸이 날래서 상대가 잡지 못해요.
examples.en: That player is so nimble that opponents can't catch him.
He caught the ball with a swift move.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 다람쥐처럼 날래게 나무를 탔어요.
examples.en: The child climbed the tree swiftly like a squirrel.
If your hands are quick, cooking finishes fast too.

examples.ko: 날래지 못한 저는 항상 늦게 도착해요.
examples.en: I'm not quick, so I always arrive late.

explain: '빠르다'가 속도 전반을 말한다면 '날래다'는 몸이나 손의 움직임이 재빠르다는 느낌이에요. 대화에서는 '빠르다', '재빠르다'를 쓰기도 하고, 불규칙 없이 '날래요', '날랜'으로 활용해요.

phrases.en: The quick cat caught the mouse in an instant.
phrases.nuance_ko: '날래다'를 '-ㄴ' 형태로 바꿔 명사를 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form of 날래다 that describes a noun.

phrases.example: 그 아이는 몸이 날래서 나무도 잘 타요.
phrases.en: That child is nimble and climbs trees well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸의 움직임이 재빠르다는 뜻으로 가장 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural pairing for quick bodily movement.

phrases.en: The clerk took the order quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '날래다'보다 대화에서 더 자주 쓰는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word used more often in conversation than 날래다.

explain_en: While '빠르다' covers speed in general, '날래다' feels like quick movement of the body or hands. In conversation people may also say '빠르다' or '재빠르다', and it conjugates regularly: '날래요', '날랜'.

en: to be quick; to be nimble; to be swift

examples.ko: 저 고양이는 정말 날쌔서 잡을 수가 없어요.
examples.en: That cat is so quick that I can't catch it.
That player's body is very nimble.
A nimble squirrel climbed up the tree.
My younger brother ran over swiftly and caught the ball.
I'm not fast on my feet, but I run to the end.
A kid who looked nimble ran out first.

explain: '빠르다'는 속도 전반에 쓰지만 '날쌔다'는 사람이나 동물의 몸놀림이 재빠르고 가벼울 때 써요. 그래서 자동차나 인터넷 속도에는 '날쌔다'를 쓰지 않아요. 반대 느낌은 '굼뜨다'이고, 비슷한 말로 '날래다'도 있어요.

phrases.en: The nimble cat caught the mouse.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주는 형태이고, 동물이나 사람에게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used before a noun, for animals or people.

phrases.en: He nimbly climbed over the wall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동작을 꾸밀 때 '날쌔게'로 바꿔 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Changes to 날쌔게 to describe an action.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is quick on their feet and ran over right away.
phrases.nuance_ko: '날쌔다'와 비슷한 말이고, 주로 몸놀림이 빠르다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word to 날쌔다, mostly used for quick body movements.
phrases.en_equiv: to be quick on one's feet

explain_en: '빠르다' (fast) works for speed in general, but '날쌔다' is for the quick, light movements of a person or animal. So you don't use it for cars or internet speed. The opposite feeling is '굼뜨다' (slow, sluggish), and '날래다' is a similar word.

t90.ax: That player's body is very nimble.

examples.en: He honestly admitted his own incompetence.
I was so ashamed of my own incompetence that I cried.

examples.ko: 상사의 무능력 때문에 팀 전체가 고생했어요.
examples.en: The whole team suffered because of the boss's incompetence.
That politician was criticized for incompetence.
Faced with repeated failures, I felt incompetent.

examples.ko: 무능력은 아니고 단지 경험이 부족할 뿐이에요.
examples.en: It's not incompetence, just a lack of experience.

explain: '능력이 없다'보다 딱딱하고 평가하는 느낌이 강해서, 사람을 향해 쓰면 꽤 심한 비난으로 들려요. 비슷한 '무능'도 있고, 부드럽게 말할 때는 '능력이 부족하다'라고 해요. 자기 자신에 대해 말할 때 많이 써요.

phrases.en: At first I felt that I was incompetent.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무능력'을 형용사로 쓴 말로 평가하는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective form, with a strongly judging tone.

phrases.example: 제가 아직 능력이 부족해서 도움이 필요해요.
phrases.en: My skills are still lacking, so I need help.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무능력'보다 부드럽게 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer way to say it than 무능력.

phrases.en: After failing, he blamed his own incompetence.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 자신을 책망할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when blaming oneself.

explain_en: Fuller form of (무능); more literal, stressing the lack of ability itself. It is stiffer and more judgmental than '능력이 없다', so aimed at a person it can sound like harsh criticism. There is also the similar '무능', and a softer way to say it is '능력이 부족하다'. It is often used when talking about oneself.

t90.ax: He honestly admitted his own incompetence.

examples.en: The color of the outfit and the shoes clash.
In this room the furniture and wallpaper don't go together.
A mismatch between words and actions lowers trust.

examples.ko: 새 건물이 주변 마을과 부조화를 보여서 말이 많아요.
examples.en: The new building looks out of place next to the village, so people are talking.
The music and the video clashed, so it felt awkward.
Even in the mismatch, there is a certain charm.

explain: '조화'의 반대말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '안 어울리다'가 더 자연스럽고, '부조화'는 글이나 설명에서 많이 써요. 색이나 모양뿐 아니라 말과 행동이 맞지 않을 때도 써요.

phrases.en: I feel a disharmony in the colors of this painting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어울리지 않는 느낌을 받았다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you sense that things do not go well together.

phrases.example: 말과 행동의 부조화 때문에 사람들이 그를 믿지 않아요.
phrases.en: People don't trust him because of the gap between his words and actions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색이나 모양이 아니라 말과 행동이 맞지 않을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used when words and actions do not match, rather than colors or shapes.

phrases.en: These shoes don't go with the outfit.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부조화'보다 일상 대화에서 훨씬 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Much more natural in everyday speech than '부조화'.

explain_en: It is the opposite of '조화' (harmony). In daily talk '안 어울리다' sounds more natural, while '부조화' is common in writing and explanations. It covers not only colors and shapes but also words and actions that don't match.

examples.en: The glass fell on the floor and shattered into pieces.

examples.ko: 시험에 떨어져서 내 계획이 산산조각 났어요.
examples.en: I failed the exam, and my plans were shattered.

examples.ko: 화가 나서 편지를 산산조각 찢어 버렸어요.
examples.en: I got angry and tore the letter into tiny pieces.
The window smashed into pieces from the impact.

examples.ko: 산산조각 난 도자기를 다시 붙이는 데 한 달이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a month to glue the shattered pottery back together.

examples.ko: 아이가 장난감 로봇을 산산조각으로 부숴 놓았어요.
examples.en: The child smashed the toy robot to bits.

explain: '산산조각이 나다', '산산조각 내다'처럼 말하고, 물건이 여러 조각으로 깨질 때 써요. 꿈, 계획, 희망, 믿음처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것이 완전히 무너질 때도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: My phone screen shattered into pieces.
phrases.nuance_ko: 저절로 깨지거나 무너졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something breaks or collapses on its own.

phrases.en: The child smashed the toy to pieces.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누군가가 일부러 또는 실수로 깨뜨렸을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone smashes something, on purpose or by accident.

phrases.example: 그 소식에 내 꿈이 산산이 부서졌어요.
phrases.en: My dream was shattered by that news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 희망이 무너질 때 글에서도 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used, including in writing, when dreams or hopes collapse.

explain_en: It is used as '산산조각이 나다' or '산산조각 내다' for things breaking into many pieces. It is also common for intangible things such as dreams, plans, hopes and trust being completely destroyed.
